questions.prompt: A hockey team trails by 1 goal with 2 minutes left, and its only goal is to avoid losing, which requires tying. Keeping the goalie gives a 0.08 chance of tying; pulling the goalie for an extra skater gives a 0.20 chance (allowing another goal still means a loss, as before). By how many percentage points does pulling the goalie raise the chance of tying, and how many times as large is that chance?

choices.text: Pull the goalie: it gives the better chance of avoiding a loss.
Keep the goalie: allowing another goal would be worse.

questions.prompt: A company can test 2 or 5 parts from each box of 10 (2 defective). With 2 tested, P(missing both defectives) = 28/45; with 5 tested, it is 2/9. Which is correct?
questions.prompt_markup: A company can test 2 or 5 parts from each box of 10 (2 defective). With 2 tested, P(missing both defectives) = 28/45; with 5 tested, it is 2/9. Which is correct?

choices.text: Testing 5 parts lowers the chance of missing the defects.
Testing 5 parts always finds both defects.
Testing 2 parts finds the defects more often.
The number tested does not change anything.

questions.correct_answer: Testing 5 parts lowers the chance of missing the defects.
questions.grading_note: With 5 tested, P(no defective found) = 8C5/10C5 = 56/252 = 2/9, less than 28/45.

questions.prompt: On a test, each question has 4 choices and one correct answer: +1 point if correct, -1/3 point if wrong, 0 if blank. A guess picks at random among the choices still in play. Which statement about strategy is correct?
questions.prompt_markup: On a test, each question has 4 choices and one correct answer: +1 point if correct, -1/3 point if wrong, 0 if blank. A guess picks at random among the choices still in play. Which statement about strategy is correct?

choices.text: A blind guess averages -1/12, less than a blank, so never guess without eliminating.
A blind guess and a blank both average 0; a guess after one elimination averages 1/9.
Eliminating one wrong choice leaves the average score of a guess at 0.
A blind guess averages 1/4, more than a blank, so guess on every question.

questions.correct_answer: A blind guess and a blank both average 0; a guess after one elimination averages 1/9.
questions.grading_note: Blind: 1/4 - (3/4)(1/3) = 0, the same as a blank (so blind guessing neither helps nor hurts on average). After one elimination: 1/3 - (2/3)(1/3) = 1/9. The others give wrong expected values.
